title: THE SEVERITY OF REBELLION AGAINST GOD

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing with their wives, children and little ones at the entrances to their tents. Then Moses said, "This is how you will know that the Lord has sent me to do all these things and that it was not my idea: If these men die a natural death and suffer the fate of all mankind, then the Lord has not sent me. But if the Lord brings about something totally new, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them, with everything that belongs to them, and they go down alive into the realm of the dead, then you will know that these men have treated the Lord with contempt." — Num 16:27-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a hard passage, and we should not soften it or hurry past it. Moses announces an extraordinary judgment: the earth itself will open and swallow the rebels. It is a sobering, even frightening scene, and it is meant to be. We must let it teach us the seriousness of rebellion against God without letting it distort our picture of His character.

Moses makes clear what is really at stake. This was never a mere personality clash between him and Korah. The test would prove whether Moses truly spoke for God. And the deepest issue is named plainly: "these men have treated the Lord with contempt." Their rebellion was not against a man; it was scorn poured out on God Himself.

Under the old covenant, at this foundational moment for the nation, God sometimes displayed His holiness in visible, immediate judgment, teaching Israel that He is not to be trifled with. We do not see such dramatic judgments today in the same way — we live in an age of God's patience, where He "is patient... not wanting anyone to perish." But the underlying truth has not changed: contempt for God is deadly serious, and rebellion against Him leads to death.

We should let this sober us, but not crush us. For here is the gospel against a dark sky: we too have treated God with contempt in our sin and deserve judgment — yet Christ went down into death in our place. He was swallowed by the grave so that we could be lifted to life. The judgment these men faced is the judgment Jesus bore for all who trust Him. What terror for the rebel; what mercy for the redeemed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you take rebellion against God as seriously as this passage does?
2. How do you hold together God's severity here and His patience today?
3. How does Christ bearing our judgment change how you read this scene?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Father, teach me to take Your holiness seriously and never to treat You with contempt. Thank You for Your patience, and thank You above all that Christ went down into death so that I could rise to life. Keep my heart humble and reverent before You. Amen.
